# Structural matching: entities can veto a wording match

Status: approved direction (2026-11-06), follow-up to
[structure over prose](2026-11-06-structure-over-prose-design.md) (D22). Plan in
[`../plans/2026-11-06-structural-matching.md`](../plans/2026-11-06-structural-matching.md).

## Problem

After the structure-over-prose work, three write-path decisions still read identity from
sentence wording or from the `kind` label:

1. **Duplicate detection** (`store._apply`). A new memory whose embedding is within
   `DUPLICATE_SCORE` of a current one (same dates) only reinforces that one and is never saved.
   The check also runs against memories stored earlier in the same extraction. Calibration's
   own NO pairs ("Maya lives in Boston" / "...in Seattle", "went running" / "went swimming")
   depend on the cut alone. If a new extraction model words things more alike, a different
   fact is merged away and lost, and no error is raised.
2. **The forget tombstone** (`store.forget`, `store._tombstones`). Within an episode, a new
   memory whose embedding is within `FORGOTTEN_SCORE` of a forgotten one is dropped. Its NO
   pairs ("Jordan moved to Denver" / "Alex is moving to Denver") are other true things said in
   the same conversation. The same drift drops them.
3. **The trip guard** (`store._apply`). A one-at-a-time relation (`lives_in`) is ignored when
   only a `kind == "status"` memory mentions its target. If the model files "I'm in Denver
   this week" as an `event` with an expiry, the guard misses it and the trip ends the real
   home. Pruning had exactly this flaw and was fixed by reading `valid_until` (D4 of the
   earlier spec).

## Principle

Merging two different things loses data. Splitting one thing into two only leaves a
near-copy. So structure gets a **veto**: wording similarity may decide a match only when the
graph agrees it could be the same thing. Where the graph can't tell, behaviour stays as it is
today.

## Design

### S1. The entity veto
An old memory (stored, stored earlier in this extraction, or a tombstone) can match a new
one only if **every entity the old one is ABOUT, other than the user, is also in the new
one's ABOUT**. The user node never counts.

- "Maya lives in Boston" {Maya, Boston} cannot match "Maya lives in Seattle" {Maya, Seattle}.
- "went running" {running} cannot match "went swimming" {swimming}. Activities are entities
  after D2 of the earlier spec.
- "Logan loves Minecraft" {Logan} still matches the re-read {Logan, Minecraft}, so a
  re-extraction still backfills entities onto the old memory (an existing test).
- Two memories about only the user ("likes coffee" / "likes tea") have nothing to veto with.
  Wording still decides there, as today. That is a stated limit, not a regression.
- If the extractor drops an entity it named before, the new memory is stored as a near-copy
  instead of reinforcing. This is accepted because it's the safe direction.

`kind` is **not** part of the veto. A label slip should not change identity (D22).

### S2. Tombstones carry entities
`forget()` records the forgotten memory's non-user ABOUT entity ids on the `Forgotten` node
(`about`). `_tombstones()` returns each vector with its id set, and S1 applies. A tombstone
with no `about` (made before this change) has an empty set, so it vetoes nothing, which is
today's behaviour.

### S3. "Temporary" for the trip guard is an expiry
The guard's temporary names come from memories with an expiry: `clock.parse_until(...)` is
not None. Lasting names come from memories without one. A status still gets its default
expiry in `clock.parse_until`. That is now the only place `kind` decides "temporary", and
it's the right place, since a status is short by definition.

### S4. Scenario checks test structure, not wording
Three LLM scenario checks failed on correct behaviour, on gemini-3.8-flash: a run said
"getting married", not "wedding" (fixed on the earlier branch); Coach said "base for
Chicago", not "race"; and a gym status that was correctly stored, consolidated and then
pruned was gone by the time the end-of-run check looked. Checks read the graph's structure
(the `gym` activity, `due_on`, `valid_until`) or what the run recorded when it happened. Run
keeps the store's write logs (`Run.logs`), so a check can see what was stored before pruning.
Reply checks accept any word that refers to the right thing ("Chicago" for the race).

## Out of scope (recorded)
- **Entity matching** (`resolve_entity`). It is already structural first (the extractor's
  `ref` id, then an exact name or alias). The vector fallback needs both `entity_match` and
  `name_match` to agree, and the one-person-role rule (one mother) merges by graph structure.
  The next step would be relation-aware matching. It is bigger and is not needed for the
  bugs above.
- **The sensitive-recall floor.** Recall is fuzzy by nature (D22 keeps similarity there).
  Recalling sensitive memories about entities the message names is a recall feature, not an
  identity fix.
- **"step" in `r.said`.** This needs a step-relation type in the ontology, which is an
  ontology change.
"}

"""Private to the persona that heard it: asked ("just between us"), or sensitive.
        Boundaries are never private: a boundary set with one persona protects with all."""
        return mem.kind != "boundary" and (mem.private or mem.sensitive)

    @traced("store.apply", "CHAIN")
    def apply(self, ex: Extraction, episode_id: str | None = None, today: dt.date | None = None) -> list[str]:
        """Store one extraction, all or nothing (one transaction). Returns a log of what changed."""
        return self._write(lambda: self._apply(ex, episode_id, today))

    def _apply(self, ex: Extraction, episode_id: str | None, today: dt.date | None) -> list[str]:
        today = today or dt.date.today()
        now = clock.now_for(today)
        q = partial(self._q, now=now)
        log: list[str] = []
        known: dict[str, str] = {}
        self.forgotten_terms: list[str] = []  # names forgotten by this call (the graph redacts its thread)
        self.written_ids: list[str] = []      # memories created or reinforced by this call
        self.entity_log = []
        for ent in ex.entities:
            eid = self.resolve_entity(ent.name, ent.kind, ent.aliases, ent.summary, ent.ref, ent.new,
                                      ent.corrected)
            for n in [ent.name, *ent.aliases, *([ent.ref] if ent.ref else [])]:
                if known.get(n.lower(), eid) != eid:  # two different Sams in one extraction
                    log.append(f"warning: '{n}' names two entities here; references to it go to the last one")
                known[n.lower()] = eid
            if ent.new and not ent.ref:
                log.append(f"new entity {ent.name} ({eid}), distinct from the known {ent.name}")
        log += self.entity_log

        # Relations go through the ontology: normalize the type, check its range, then apply
        # its rules (cardinality "one" ends the previous edge; "ended" ends the whole lineage).
        resolved = []
        for rel in ex.relations:
            a, b = self._lookup(rel.source, known), self._lookup(rel.target, known)
            if a and b and a != b:
                canon, how, flip = ontology.normalize(rel.type)
                if how == "group":
                    log.append(f"rejected {rel.source} -{rel.type}-> {rel.target}: '{rel.type}' is a "
                               "group in the ontology, not a relation type")
                    continue
                resolved.append((rel, *((b, a) if flip else (a, b)), canon, "flipped" if flip else how))
        # Guard (Lesson 13): a one-at-a-time relation (lives_in) to something that only a
        # temporary status mentions is a trip, not a move. Applying it would end the real home.
        temporary = {n.lower() for m in ex.memories if m.kind == "status" for n in m.about}
        lasting = {n.lower() for m in ex.memories if m.kind != "status" for n in m.about}
        kept = []
        for item in resolved:
            rel, canon = item[0], item[3]
            target = rel.target.lower()
            if (not rel.ended and ontology.rule(canon, "cardinality") == "one"
                    and target in temporary and target not in lasting):
                log.append(f"ignored {rel.source} -{canon}-> {rel.target}: only a temporary status "
                           "mentions it (a trip, not a move)")
                continue
            kept.append(item)
        resolved = kept
        # Lesson 16: a relation to someone only PRIVATE memories mention is private too,
        # or another persona's people list would give it away.
        private_names = {n.lower() for m in ex.memories if self._private(m) for n in m.about}
        shared_names = {n.lower() for m in ex.memories if not self._private(m) for n in m.about}
        linking = {(a, b, canon) for rel, a, b, canon, _ in resolved if not rel.ended}
        linked: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []  # edges this extraction (re)asserts: evidence below
        for rel, a, b, canon, how in resolved:
            if rel.ended and (a, b, canon) in linking:
                continue  # "ended X" + "linked X" in one go: keep it linked
            info = q("MATCH (a:Entity {id: $a}), (b:Entity {id: $b}) RETURN a.name AS a, b.name AS b, b.kind AS kind",
                           a=a, b=b)[0]
            src, dst = ("user" if a == self.user else info["a"]), info["b"]
            said = f" (said '{rel.type}')" if how in ("synonym", "flipped") else ""
            if not rel.ended and a == self.user and canon in one_person_roles() and not is_role_name(dst):
                # "Mom" first, "my mother Linda" later, and the extractor didn't say they're the
                # same: someone has one mother (or partner), so a role-named one IS Linda.
                for y in q(
                    """
                    MATCH (:User {id: $user})-[r:RELATED]->(y:Entity) WHERE y.id <> $b AND r.until IS NULL
                      AND r.type IN $types AND NOT toLower(coalesce(r.said, '')) CONTAINS 'step'
                    RETURN y.id AS id, y.name AS name
                    """,
                    b=b, types=sorted(ontology.lineage(canon) | {canon}),
                ):
                    if is_role_name(y["name"]) and "step" not in rel.type.lower():
                        self.merge_entities(b, y["id"])
                        known = {k: (b if v == y["id"] else v) for k, v in known.items()}
                        log.append(f"merged {y['name']} into {dst} (one {canon})")
            if rel.ended:  # breakup, moved away, left a job: keep the edge as history
                ended = q(
                    """
                    MATCH (a:Entity {id: $a})-[r:RELATED]->(b:Entity {id: $b})
                    WHERE r.until IS NULL AND r.type IN $types
                    SET r.until = $today RETURN r.type AS type
                    """,
                    a=a, b=b, types=sorted(ontology.lineage(canon) | {canon}), today=today,
                )
                if ended:
                    log.append(f"ended {src} -{'/'.join(e['type'] for e in ended)}-> {dst}{said}")
                continue
            if not ontology.range_ok(canon, info["kind"]):
                log.append(f"rejected {src} -{canon}-> {dst}: {canon} needs a {'/'.join(ontology.rule(canon, 'range'))}, "
                           f"{dst} is a {info['kind']}")
                continue
            if how == "new":
                hint = ontology.propose_type(self.driver, canon, f"{src} -{rel.type}-> {dst}")
                log.append(f"new relation type '{canon}' proposed for the ontology (closest: {hint})")
            for x in q(  # likes <-> dislikes: the new one ends the opposite edge to the same target
                """
                MATCH (a:Entity {id: $a})-[r:RELATED]->(b:Entity {id: $b})
                WHERE r.until IS NULL AND r.type IN $types
                SET r.until = $today RETURN r.type AS type
                """,
                a=a, b=b, types=ontology.rule(canon, "exclusive") or [], today=today,
            ):
                log.append(f"ended {src} -{x['type']}-> {dst} (now {canon})")
            if ontology.rule(canon, "cardinality") == "one":  # e.g. one lives_in at a time
                moved = q(
                    """
                    MATCH (a:Entity {id: $a})-[r:RELATED]->(other:Entity)
                    WHERE r.until IS NULL AND r.type IN $types AND (other.id <> $b OR r.type <> $type)
                    SET r.until = $today RETURN other.name AS name, r.type AS type
                    """,
                    a=a, b=b, type=canon, types=sorted(ontology.lineage(canon) | {canon}), today=today,
                )
                for m in moved:
                    log.append(f"ended {src} -{m['type']}-> {m['name']} (one {canon} at a time)")
            changed = q(
                """
                MATCH (a:Entity {id: $a}), (b:Entity {id: $b})
                MERGE (a)-[r:RELATED {type: $type}]->(b)
                WITH r, r.updated_at IS NULL OR r.until IS NOT NULL AS changed
                SET r.since = coalesce($since, r.since), r.updated_at = $now, r.until = null,
                    r.said = $said_as, r.agent = coalesce(r.agent, $agent),
                    r.private = $private AND coalesce(r.private, true)  // once shared, stays shared
                RETURN changed
                """,
                a=a, b=b, type=canon, since=rel.since, now=now, said_as=rel.type,
                private=rel.target.lower() in private_names and rel.target.lower() not in shared_names,
            )[0]["changed"]
            linked.append((a, b, canon))
            if changed:  # only log new or re-activated links
                log.append(f"linked {src} -{canon}-> {dst}{said}")

        evidence: list[tuple[str, set[str]]] = []  # (memory id, entity ids it is about)
        retired_pairs: list[tuple[str, str | None]] = []  # (retired memory, its replacement)
        for mid in ex.invalidate:
            if q(
                """
                MATCH (m:Memory {id: $id, user: $user}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL
                SET m.invalidated_at = $now RETURN m.text AS text

"""Lesson 9 — the memory write path, WITHOUT the LLM.

The extractor (LLM) and the store (code) meet at one typed object: `Extraction`. Hand-write
the Extraction a model *would* return and you can test every storage rule exactly and for
free. The LLM half is graded separately in test_11_extraction_evals.py.
"""
import datetime as dt

import pytest
from pydantic import ValidationError

from companion.models import EntityOut, Extraction, MemoryOut, RelationOut

T = dt.date(2026, 11, 5)


def mem(text, kind="fact", **kw):
    return MemoryOut(text=text, kind=kind, importance=kw.pop("importance", 6), **kw)


def current(store):
    return {m["text"] for m in store.memories()}


def test_schema_rejects_bad_llm_output():
    # Validation is the first eval: a malformed answer fails loudly instead of corrupting data.
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        MemoryOut(text="x", kind="gossip", importance=5)
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        MemoryOut(text="x", kind="fact", importance=11)


def test_entities_relations_and_memories_are_linked(store):
    log = store.apply(Extraction(
        entities=[EntityOut(name="Maya", kind="person", aliases=["my sister"])],
        relations=[RelationOut(source="user", target="Maya", type="sister")],
        memories=[mem("Pytest's sister Maya lives in Denver", about=["Maya"])],
    ), today=T)
    assert "linked user -sister-> Maya" in log
    about = store._q("""MATCH (m:Memory {user:$user})-[:ABOUT]->(e:Entity {name:'Maya'})
                        RETURN m.text AS text""")
    assert [a["text"] for a in about] == ["Pytest's sister Maya lives in Denver"]


def test_aliases_resolve_to_the_same_entity(store):
    store.apply(Extraction(entities=[EntityOut(name="Maya", kind="person", aliases=["my sister"])]), today=T)
    store.apply(Extraction(entities=[EntityOut(name="my sister", kind="person")]), today=T)
    assert len(store._q("MATCH (e:Entity {user:$user, kind:'person'}) WHERE NOT e:User RETURN e")) == 1


def test_duplicate_memory_is_reinforced_not_copied(store):
    ex = Extraction(memories=[mem("Pytest loves rock climbing", "preference")])
    store.apply(ex, today=T)
    log = store.apply(ex, today=T)
    assert log[0].startswith("reinforced")
    assert len(store.memories()) == 1


def test_same_text_different_date_is_not_a_duplicate(store):
    store.apply(Extraction(memories=[mem("Dentist appointment", "plan", due_on="2026-11-12")]), today=T)
    store.apply(Extraction(memories=[mem("Dentist appointment", "plan", due_on="2026-11-17")]), today=T)
    assert len(store.memories()) == 2


def test_supersedes_retires_the_old_fact_and_keeps_history(store):
    store.apply(Extraction(memories=[mem("Pytest lives in Austin")]), today=T)
    [old] = store.memories()
    store.apply(Extraction(memories=[mem("Pytest lives in Chicago", supersedes=[old["id"]])]), today=T)
    assert current(store) == {"Pytest lives in Chicago"}
    history = store._q("""MATCH (:Memory {user:$user})-[:SUPERSEDES]->(o:Memory)
                          RETURN o.text AS text, o.invalidated_at IS NOT NULL AS retired""")
    assert history == [{"text": "Pytest lives in Austin", "retired": True}]


def test_ids_from_another_user_are_ignored(store, driver):
    # The extractor only ever sees this user's ids, but the store must not trust that.
    driver.execute_query("CREATE (:Memory {id:'m_other', user:'user:someone-else', text:'secret'})")
    try:

                    continue
                resolved.append((rel, *((b, a) if flip else (a, b)), canon, "flipped" if flip else how))
        # Guard (Lesson 13): a one-at-a-time relation (lives_in) to something that only a
        # temporary status mentions is a trip, not a move. Applying it would end the real home.
        temporary = {n.lower() for m in ex.memories if m.kind == "status" for n in m.about}
        lasting = {n.lower() for m in ex.memories if m.kind != "status" for n in m.about}
        kept = []
        for item in resolved:
            rel, canon = item[0], item[3]
            target = rel.target.lower()
            if (not rel.ended and ontology.rule(canon, "cardinality") == "one"
                    and target in temporary and target not in lasting):
                log.append(f"ignored {rel.source} -{canon}-> {rel.target}: only a temporary status "
                           "mentions it (a trip, not a move)")
                continue
            kept.append(item)
        resolved = kept
        # Lesson 16: a relation to someone only PRIVATE memories mention is private too,
        # or another persona's people list would give it away.
        private_names = {n.lower() for m in ex.memories if self._private(m) for n in m.about}
        shared_names = {n.lower() for m in ex.memories if not self._private(m) for n in m.about}
        linking = {(a, b, canon) for rel, a, b, canon, _ in resolved if not rel.ended}
        linked: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []  # edges this extraction (re)asserts: evidence below
        for rel, a, b, canon, how in resolved:
            if rel.ended and (a, b, canon) in linking:
                continue  # "ended X" + "linked X" in one go: keep it linked
            info = q("MATCH (a:Entity {id: $a}), (b:Entity {id: $b}) RETURN a.name AS a, b.name AS b, b.kind AS kind",
                           a=a, b=b)[0]
            src, dst = ("user" if a == self.user else info["a"]), info["b"]
            said = f" (said '{rel.type}')" if how in ("synonym", "flipped") else ""
            if not rel.ended and a == self.user and canon in one_person_roles() and not is_role_name(dst):
                # "Mom" first, "my mother Linda" later, and the extractor didn't say they're the
                # same: someone has one mother (or partner), so a role-named one IS Linda.
                for y in q(
                    """
                    MATCH (:User {id: $user})-[r:RELATED]->(y:Entity) WHERE y.id <> $b AND r.until IS NULL
                      AND r.type IN $types AND NOT toLower(coalesce(r.said, '')) CONTAINS 'step'
                    RETURN y.id AS id, y.name AS name
                    """,
                    b=b, types=sorted(ontology.lineage(canon) | {canon}),
                ):
                    if is_role_name(y["name"]) and "step" not in rel.type.lower():
                        self.merge_entities(b, y["id"])
                        known = {k: (b if v == y["id"] else v) for k, v in known.items()}
                        log.append(f"merged {y['name']} into {dst} (one {canon})")
            if rel.ended:  # breakup, moved away, left a job: keep the edge as history
                ended = q(
                    """
                    MATCH (a:Entity {id: $a})-[r:RELATED]->(b:Entity {id: $b})
                    WHERE r.until IS NULL AND r.type IN $types
                    SET r.until = $today RETURN r.type AS type
                    """,
                    a=a, b=b, types=sorted(ontology.lineage(canon) | {canon}), today=today,
                )
                if ended:
                    log.append(f"ended {src} -{'/'.join(e['type'] for e in ended)}-> {dst}{said}")
                continue
            if not ontology.range_ok(canon, info["kind"]):
                log.append(f"rejected {src} -{canon}-> {dst}: {canon} needs a {'/'.join(ontology.rule(canon, 'range'))}, "
                           f"{dst} is a {info['kind']}")
                continue
            if how == "new":
                hint = ontology.propose_type(self.driver, canon, f"{src} -{rel.type}-> {dst}")
                log.append(f"new relation type '{canon}' proposed for the ontology (closest: {hint})")
            for x in q(  # likes <-> dislikes: the new one ends the opposite edge to the same target
                """
                MATCH (a:Entity {id: $a})-[r:RELATED]->(b:Entity {id: $b})
                WHERE r.until IS NULL AND r.type IN $types
                SET r.until = $today RETURN r.type AS type
                """,
                a=a, b=b, types=ontology.rule(canon, "exclusive") or [], today=today,
            ):
                log.append(f"ended {src} -{x['type']}-> {dst} (now {canon})")
            if ontology.rule(canon, "cardinality") == "one":  # e.g. one lives_in at a time
                moved = q(
                    """
                    MATCH (a:Entity {id: $a})-[r:RELATED]->(other:Entity)
                    WHERE r.until IS NULL AND r.type IN $types AND (other.id <> $b OR r.type <> $type)
                    SET r.until = $today RETURN other.name AS name, r.type AS type
                    """,
                    a=a, b=b, type=canon, types=sorted(ontology.lineage(canon) | {canon}), today=today,
                )

                    log.append(f"ended {src} -{m['type']}-> {m['name']} (one {canon} at a time)")
            changed = q(
                """
                MATCH (a:Entity {id: $a}), (b:Entity {id: $b})
                MERGE (a)-[r:RELATED {type: $type}]->(b)
                WITH r, r.updated_at IS NULL OR r.until IS NOT NULL AS changed
                SET r.since = coalesce($since, r.since), r.updated_at = $now, r.until = null,
                    r.said = $said_as, r.agent = coalesce(r.agent, $agent),
                    r.private = $private AND coalesce(r.private, true)  // once shared, stays shared
                RETURN changed

                a=a, b=b, type=canon, since=rel.since, now=now, said_as=rel.type,
                private=rel.target.lower() in private_names and rel.target.lower() not in shared_names,
            )[0]["changed"]
            linked.append((a, b, canon))
            if changed:  # only log new or re-activated links
                log.append(f"linked {src} -{canon}-> {dst}{said}")

        retired_pairs: list[tuple[str, str | None]] = []  # (retired memory, its replacement)
        for mid in ex.invalidate:

                """
                MATCH (m:Memory {id: $id, user: $user}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL
                SET m.invalidated_at = $now RETURN m.text AS text

            ):
                log.append(f"retired {mid}")
                retired_pairs.append((mid, None))

        # same due date) is still on: smaller models have "completed" a plan that was only moved.
        restated_ids = sorted({sid for m in ex.memories for sid in m.supersedes})

                    if m.kind == "plan" and (d := _to_date(m.due_on))]
        for mid in ex.completed_plans:
            [row] = q(
                """
                OPTIONAL MATCH (m:Memory {id: $id, user: $user, kind: 'plan', status: 'open'})
                WITH m, m IS NOT NULL AND (m.id IN $ids OR any(r IN $restated
                     WHERE r.due = m.due_on AND r.text = toLower(trim(m.text)))) AS restated
                FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN m IS NOT NULL AND NOT restated THEN [1] ELSE [] END |
                    SET m.status = 'done')
                RETURN m IS NOT NULL AS found, restated
                """, id=mid, ids=restated_ids, restated=restated,

                """

                  AND """ + visible("node") + """

                  // same but is a real correction; an identical "replacement" is just a duplicate
                  AND coalesce(node.due_on, date('1900-01-01')) = coalesce($due, date('1900-01-01'))
                  AND coalesce(node.occurred_on, date('1900-01-01')) = coalesce($occurred, date('1900-01-01'))
                RETURN node.id AS id, node.text AS text, score ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 1
                """,
                vec=vec, due=_to_date(mem.due_on), occurred=_to_date(mem.occurred_on),
            )
            dup = [n for n in nearest if n["score"] >= DUPLICATE_SCORE]
            if dup:  # already known: reinforce instead of storing a near-copy
                q(
                    """
                    MATCH (m:Memory {id: $id})
                    SET m.access_count = coalesce(m.access_count, 0) + 1, m.last_confirmed = $now,
                        m.valid_until = CASE WHEN m.valid_until IS NULL OR $until IS NULL THEN m.valid_until
                                             WHEN $until > m.valid_until THEN $until ELSE m.valid_until END,
                        m.importance = CASE WHEN $imp > m.importance THEN $imp ELSE m.importance END
                    """,
                    id=dup[0]["id"], imp=mem.importance, until=until,
                )
                # ...and is about every entity it names now, not only those named before (a
                # re-read under new rules: "Logan loves Minecraft" gains Minecraft)
                q("MATCH (m:Memory {id: $id}) UNWIND $about AS eid MATCH (e:Entity {id: eid}) MERGE (m)-[:ABOUT]->(e)",
                  id=dup[0]["id"], about=[eid for n in mem.about if (eid := self._lookup(n, known))])
                log.append(f"reinforced {dup[0]['id']} \"{dup[0]['text']}\" "
                           f"(similarity {dup[0]['score']:.3f} ≥ {DUPLICATE_SCORE})")
                self.written_ids.append(dup[0]["id"])
                evidence.append((dup[0]["id"], {eid for n in (mem.about or ["user"]) if (eid := self._lookup(n, known))}))
                # The near-copy may still be a correction ("brother is Leo" superseding "...Theo"):
                # retire what it replaces, or the wrong memory stays current.
                for old in q(
                    """
                    MATCH (keep:Memory {id: $keep}), (old:Memory {user: $user})
                    WHERE old.id IN $ids AND old.id <> $keep AND old.invalidated_at IS NULL
                    SET old.invalidated_at = $now MERGE (keep)-[:SUPERSEDES]->(old) RETURN old.id AS id
                    """,
                    keep=dup[0]["id"], ids=mem.supersedes, now=now,
                ):

                    retired_pairs.append((old["id"], dup[0]["id"]))…541 tokens truncated…d %H:%M})"

            why = (f"  [new: closest known {nearest[0]['score']:.3f} < {DUPLICATE_SCORE}]" if nearest
                   else "  [new: nothing similar with the same dates]")
            log.append(f"+ [{mem.kind}] {mem.text}{flags}" + (f"  (replaces {', '.join(retired)})" if retired else "") + why)

        # Provenance: each edge lists the memories that support it, those about BOTH its ends
        # ("Maya also lives in Boston" is no evidence for the user's own lives_in Boston). When
        # they are all retired with no heir, the edge ends with them.
        for a, b, canon in linked:

            if ids:
                q("""
                  MATCH (:Entity {id: $a})-[r:RELATED {type: $type}]->(:Entity {id: $b})
                  SET r.evidence = apoc.coll.toSet(coalesce(r.evidence, []) + $ids)
                  """, a=a, b=b, type=canon, ids=ids)
        log += self._retire_links(retired_pairs, today, skip=linked)

        for name in ex.forget_entities:  # last, so memories made this turn about them go too
            gone = self.forget_entity(name, known)
            if gone:
                self.forgotten_terms += gone["terms"]
                log.append(f"forgot {gone['name']}: {gone['memories']} memories deleted, "
                           f"{gone['turns']} turns and {gone['episodes']} summaries redacted")
        return log

"""Lesson 9 — the memory write path, WITHOUT the LLM.

The extractor (LLM) and the store (code) meet at one typed object: `Extraction`. Hand-write
the Extraction a model *would* return and you can test every storage rule exactly and for
free. The LLM half is graded separately in test_11_extraction_evals.py.
"""
import datetime as dt

import pytest
from pydantic import ValidationError

from companion.models import EntityOut, Extraction, MemoryOut, RelationOut

T = dt.date(2026, 11, 5)


def mem(text, kind="fact", **kw):
    return MemoryOut(text=text, kind=kind, importance=kw.pop("importance", 6), **kw)


def current(store):
    return {m["text"] for m in store.memories()}


def test_schema_rejects_bad_llm_output():
    # Validation is the first eval: a malformed answer fails loudly instead of corrupting data.
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        MemoryOut(text="x", kind="gossip", importance=5)
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        MemoryOut(text="x", kind="fact", importance=11)


def test_entities_relations_and_memories_are_linked(store):
    log = store.apply(Extraction(
        entities=[EntityOut(name="Maya", kind="person", aliases=["my sister"])],
        relations=[RelationOut(source="user", target="Maya", type="sister")],
        memories=[mem("Pytest's sister Maya lives in Denver", about=["Maya"])],
    ), today=T)
    assert "linked user -sister-> Maya" in log
    about = store._q("""MATCH (m:Memory {user:$user})-[:ABOUT]->(e:Entity {name:'Maya'})
                        RETURN m.text AS text""")
    assert [a["text"] for a in about] == ["Pytest's sister Maya lives in Denver"]


def test_aliases_resolve_to_the_same_entity(store):
    store.apply(Extraction(entities=[EntityOut(name="Maya", kind="person", aliases=["my sister"])]), today=T)
    store.apply(Extraction(entities=[EntityOut(name="my sister", kind="person")]), today=T)
    assert len(store._q("MATCH (e:Entity {user:$user, kind:'person'}) WHERE NOT e:User RETURN e")) == 1


def test_duplicate_memory_is_reinforced_not_copied(store):
    ex = Extraction(memories=[mem("Pytest loves rock climbing", "preference")])
    store.apply(ex, today=T)
    log = store.apply(ex, today=T)
    assert log[0].startswith("reinforced")
    assert len(store.memories()) == 1


def test_same_text_different_date_is_not_a_duplicate(store):
    store.apply(Extraction(memories=[mem("Dentist appointment", "plan", due_on="2026-11-12")]), today=T)
    store.apply(Extraction(memories=[mem("Dentist appointment", "plan", due_on="2026-11-17")]), today=T)
    assert len(store.memories()) == 2


def test_supersedes_retires_the_old_fact_and_keeps_history(store):
    store.apply(Extraction(memories=[mem("Pytest lives in Austin")]), today=T)
    [old] = store.memories()
    store.apply(Extraction(memories=[mem("Pytest lives in Chicago", supersedes=[old["id"]])]), today=T)
    assert current(store) == {"Pytest lives in Chicago"}
    history = store._q("""MATCH (:Memory {user:$user})-[:SUPERSEDES]->(o:Memory)
                          RETURN o.text AS text, o.invalidated_at IS NOT NULL AS retired""")
    assert history == [{"text": "Pytest lives in Austin", "retired": True}]


def test_ids_from_another_user_are_ignored(store, driver):
    # The extractor only ever sees this user's ids, but the store must not trust that.
    driver.execute_query("CREATE (:Memory {id:'m_other', user:'user:someone-else', text:'secret'})")
    try:
        store.apply(Extraction(invalidate=["m_other"],
                               memories=[mem("Pytest fact", supersedes=["m_other"])]), today=T)
        [r] = driver.execute_query("MATCH (m:Memory {id:'m_other'}) RETURN m.invalidated_at AS at").records
        assert r["at"] is None
    finally:
        driver.execute_query("MATCH (m:Memory {id:'m_other'}) DETACH DELETE m")

    assert (NOON.hour, NOON.minute) == (12, 0) and NOON.tzinfo is not None

    ("2026-11-18T14:00", "status", (2026, 11, 18, 14, 0)),
    ("2026-11-18", "feeling", (2026, 11, 18, 23, 59)),      # a date: the end of that day
    (None, "status", (2026, 11, 18, 15, 0)),                 # a status always ends (3 h default)
    ("2026-11-18T09:00", "status", (2026, 11, 18, 15, 0)),   # already past: default instead
    ("whenever", "status", (2026, 11, 18, 15, 0)),           # unreadable: default
    (None, "fact", None),                                    # lasting things never expire

def about_entity(run: Run, name: str, word: str, relation: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """Current memories ABOUT an entity named `name` (optionally with this relation to the user)
    whose text contains `word`."""
    return run.q(
        """
        MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user})-[:ABOUT]->(e:Entity {name: $name}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL
          AND toLower(m.text) CONTAINS toLower($word)
          AND ($rel IS NULL OR EXISTS { (:User {id: $user})-[r:RELATED {type: $rel}]->(e) })
        "situational", "Short-lived statuses expire, get a follow-up, and roll up into a habit",
        [
            (D(2026, 11, 18), ["Heading to the gym, talk later!"]),
            (D(2026, 11, 19), ["Morning! I slept terribly though."]),
            (D(2026, 11, 20), ["Just got back from the gym, my legs are dead."]),
            (D(2026, 11, 21), ["Off to the gym again after work, then dinner."]),
            (D(2026, 11, 23), ["Gym again before work today, trying to keep the streak going."]),
        ],
        [
            ("the gym was stored as a status that expires", lambda r: bool(r.q(
                "MATCH (m:Memory {user:$user}) WHERE toLower(m.text) CONTAINS 'gym' AND m.valid_until IS NOT NULL RETURN m"))),
            ("the next day nothing says they're at the gym now", lambda r: not any(
                "gym" in m["text"].lower() and m["kind"] == "status" for m in r.store.memories(today=D(2026, 11, 19)))),
            ("the next day's greeting asks about the gym", lambda r: r.mentions(r.greetings[1], "gym", "workout")),
            ("three gym visits became one lasting habit", lambda r: bool(r.q(
                """MATCH (p:Memory {user:$user}) WHERE p.invalidated_at IS NULL AND p.evidence >= 3
                     AND p.kind IN ['preference', 'fact'] AND toLower(p.text) CONTAINS 'gym' RETURN p"""))),
        ],
    ),
]


def threshold_check() -> tuple[str, bool]:
    """Every scenario run also checks that the thresholds were measured on this extraction
    model's sentences (structure-over-prose spec). Fix a failure by re-running
    `python -m companion.calibrate` and the scenarios on the new model, then updating
    `extraction_model` on the profile."""
    used, measured = config.LLM_EXTRACTION_MODEL, PROFILE.extraction_model
    return (f"thresholds measured with this extraction model ({measured} vs {used})", used == measured)


def run_scenario(driver, sc: Scenario, verbose: bool = True) -> list[tuple[str, bool]]:
    store = MemoryStore(driver, f"eval {sc.name}")
    store.wipe()
    store.user_name = "Riley"  # display name in prompts
    run = Run(store, stores={store.agent: store})
    apps = {store.agent: build_companion(store)}
    for n, (today, messages, *persona) in enumerate(sc.sessions, 1):
        if persona and persona[0] not in run.stores:  # another persona, same user
            other = MemoryStore(driver, f"eval {sc.name}", agent=persona[0])
            other.user_name = "Riley"
            run.stores[persona[0]], apps[persona[0]] = other, build_companion(other)
        store = run.stores[persona[0] if persona else run.store.agent]
        app = apps[store.agent]
        episode_id = store.start_episode(on=today)
        hello = greeting(store, today)
        seed_thread(app, episode_id, hello)
        run.greetings.append(hello)
        run.replies.append([])
        run.extracted.append([])
        if verbose:
            print(f"  -- session {n} ({today})\n  {store.agent}: {hello}")
        config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": episode_id, "today": today}}
        for text in messages:
            if verbose:
                print(f"  Riley: {text}")
            ran = False
            for update in app.stream({"messages": [HumanMessage(text)]}, config, stream_mode="updates"):
                node, out = next(iter(update.items()))
                if node == "respond":
                    run.replies[-1].append(out["messages"][-1].content)
                    if verbose:
                        print(f"  {store.agent}: {out['messages'][-1].content}")
                elif node == "remember":
                    ran = True
                    if verbose:
                        for line in out["memory_log"]:
                            print(f"     ✎ {line}")
            run.extracted[-1].append(ran)
            if verbose and not ran:
                print("     (small talk — extraction skipped)")
        for line in close_episode(store, episode_id, today):
            if verbose:
                print(f"     ✎ {line}")
    results = []
    for desc, check in sc.checks:
        try:
            ok = bool(check(run))
        except Exception as e:  # a crashing check is a failing check
            print(f"     check error: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
            ok = False
        results.append((desc, ok))
    results.append(threshold_check())
    return results


def main() -> None:
    words = [w.lower() for w in sys.argv[1:]]

### D22. Decide identity in the graph; compare prose only where meaning is fuzzy

**Chose:** decisions about *identity* read structure and typed fields, not sentence wording.
A known day lives in `occurred_on` / `due_on` / `valid_until`, not in the text (shown from
the field in prompts and the UI). An activity someone does ("gym", "running") is an `activity`
entity every memory about it is linked to. A habit is memories `ABOUT` one activity on 3+
distinct days, counted in Cypher. Pruning reads "temporary" from `valid_until`, the timeline
reads "dated" from the date fields. Each embedding profile records the extraction model its
thresholds were measured with (`Profile.extraction_model`), and every scenario run checks it.
([Lessons 9](../lessons/09-memory-write-path.md) and [13](../lessons/13-memory-over-time.md);
design notes in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-structure-over-prose-design.md`)

**Why:** the extractor is an LLM that can be swapped. When `gemma-4-31B-it` was replaced by
`gemini-3.8-flash`, the gym habit stopped forming. The new model wrote dated, longer sentences,
so no pair of gym memories reached the clustering cut (0.82, measured on undated hand-written
sentences), and a dated rock-climbing memory scored closer to a gym memory than gym memories
did to each other. It also filed one visit as a `plan`, a kind the clustering skipped. Every
threshold and every `kind` switch had the same weakness: it silently depended on how one
model words and labels things. Lowering the cut would have passed the test until the next
model change.

**Costs:** the extractor must link activities (an eval checks it); two names for one activity
that never get merged ("gym", "working out") count separately; repeated feelings with no
activity ("tired" three times) no longer roll up. Similarity thresholds remain where meaning
really is fuzzy (recall, relevance, entity matching), and those still need re-measuring after
a model change: the scenario check makes that impossible to miss.

**Alternatives:** keep clustering and re-tune the cut per extraction model (cheap now, breaks
again later); strip dates before embedding (fixes one cause of drift, not labels or wording);
let the LLM group memories into habits directly (no threshold, but no guarantee across runs).
Lowering the cut would have passed the test and broken again on the next model. The fix
moved the decision out of the wording: dates live in their fields (Lesson 9, rule 2), the
activity is an entity, and a habit is a count. The full analysis is in
[design decisions](../docs/design-decisions.md#d22).

## What the tests and evals found

- **"places" was used as a relation type.** Asking about "I'm at the airport waiting for my
  flight to Denver" produced `user -places-> Denver`, a *group heading* from the ontology list.
  Group names are now rejected in `normalize()`, and the prompt says they're headings.
- **A trip almost moved the user.** "I'm in Denver for the week" came back with
  `user -lives_in-> Denver`. Because `lives_in` is one-at-a-time (Lesson 12), that would end
  their real home. Adding a prompt *rule* didn't change the output; a prompt *example* did. A
  store guard now also ignores a one-at-a-time relation that only a status mentions.
  Again: let code back up the prompt where a mistake is costly.
- **Pruning ate the pattern.** The first version pruned a minor status after ~2 days, before
  three visits could pile up over a week. It also deleted pattern members, so the scenario's
  "evidence ≥ 3" check failed. Pruning now waits for consolidation or the window, and the
  pattern keeps an `evidence` count.
- **The as-of filter hid the scenarios' memories.** Scenario dates (late November 2026) were
  after the real today, so a default `created_at <= now` made their memories invisible. The
The `store` fixture uses its own `pytest` user and wipes it before and after each test.

A code review of the write path produced regression tests. Each one failed before its fix:
- a correction that matched an existing memory was "reinforced" and **dropped its `supersedes`**;
- forgetting "Ann" deleted *"planning an anniversary trip"* (substring match, now whole words);
- short names ("Jo") and other entities' summaries ("Kai: Jo's brother") weren't redacted;
- `/forget <id>` didn't stick: the end-of-episode pass re-read the transcript and stored the
  same fact again. A tombstone (the embedding only, no text) now blocks it for that episode;
- vector searches filtered by user *after* taking the top 5, so other users' memories could
  crowd out the real duplicate. Now they take 50, filter, then keep the top k.
- "his name is Logan" never reached the graph. The node stayed `Mark's son`: a known entity
  matched by `ref` kept its old name, and the new name wasn't even added as an alias. Found in a
  real chat; the three `placeholder`/`real_name` tests cover it.
# Glossary — overlapping terms in graph, memory and agent work
